FROM FOSTER TO FLIGHT

Expanding opportunities. Changing generations.

From Foster to Flight is a founder-led foster-youth development initiative, created from the lived experience of a former foster youth herself, to expand opportunity for young people navigating foster care, the child welfare system and life far beyond it.

Through mentorship and hands-on professional development, networking and career exploration, it is designed to build confidence, strengthen practical skills and create tangible pathways toward education, leadership and opportunity.

Aviation is offered as our signature pathway - using flight both literally and symbolically to expose youth to possibilities they may have never imagined, while expanding what they believe is possible for their own future.

OUR APPROACH

Possibility should not depend on the circumstances a young person inherited.

Young people impacted by foster care and the child welfare system deserve more than preparation for independence. They deserve the skills, relationships and access to build lives defined by possibility - not circumstance.

OUR STORY

I was once the young person this organization is designed to serve.

ASIA PAYTON
Founder | Foster Youth Advocate | Mentor

Asia Payton's childhood was shaped by survival long before it was shaped by possibility. One of six children raised in poverty by a single mother, she experienced an incarcerated father, abuse, family separation, foster care, bouncing from home to home and school to school, becoming street-affiliated and leaving high school before graduating. Her childhood was largely stripped of the stability that allows young people to simply be children. As she entered adulthood and navigated life as a young single mother, survival continued to come before dreaming - until she made the decision that where her story began would not determine where it ended.

As she stepped into motherhood, Asia continued her college education through Ace's earliest years, ultimately completing nearly four years of postsecondary education and career training.

Asia received services through the Independent Living Skills Program (ILSP) as a young girl in foster care, later returning to those same spaces to serve young people navigating experiences she had lived through firsthand - determined to make sure the youth coming behind her felt seen, supported and never left behind. She now serves as an emergency foster-care placement provider, foster-youth advocate, mentor, youth workshop facilitator and community coach. Her work extends beyond direct youth service, including social-worker training to strengthen understanding of foster-youth needs and the child welfare system. Her lived experience has also carried into professional decision-making spaces, serving as a panelist reviewing and scoring youth-serving organizations and contributing to conversations surrounding mental health, community and education - helping award $3.2 million in funding. She returned to those same rooms not simply as someone who had lived through the system, but as someone who had survived it - and came back determined to help change it.

“I don’t want young people to leave inspired for one night. I want them to leave with a person, a skill, a resource and a next step.”
- Asia Payton

As Asia continues to take flight, she is actively building her place and career in aviation - pursuing her Private Pilot Certificate through continued training and flight experience, with the ambitious goal of becoming one of the Bay Area's youngest Black women pilots. Her journey into aviation carries a larger purpose: bringing a world rarely introduced to young people impacted by foster care and the child welfare system within their reach.

“I came from the system with the odds stacked against me and discovered a world bigger than the one I was given. Now, I’m building runways for the young people coming behind me to discover just how far they can go.”
- Asia Payton

FROM POSSIBILITY TO PRACTICE

Young people should leave with more than inspiration.

Young people should leave with more than inspiration. They should leave better equipped not only for what comes next, but for the future they are working toward. From Foster to Flight creates hands-on experiences that strengthen communication, confidence, self-advocacy and professional skills while connecting young people to mentors, educators, resources, professional networks, career opportunities and a community of people invested in seeing them move forward.

The goal is not to tell young people who to become, but to equip them with the tools, access, information and relationships to decide what they want their future to look like - and take meaningful steps toward it. Through exposure to professional environments, educators and mentors, young people develop the communication, presence and professional skills to navigate unfamiliar spaces with greater confidence and preparation.

Most importantly, the experience is designed to turn exposure into action. Young people leave with an individualized action plan - clear goals, tangible next steps, identified resources and people they can turn to - so the support does not end when the program does.

IMPACT

SUCCESS IS MORE THAN SHOWING UP.

Impact is not measured by how many young people enter the room, but by what they are better equipped to do when they leave it. From Foster to Flight is designed to measure progress beyond participation - tracking the skills young people develop, the relationships and resources they gain, the action plans they create and the educational, professional and career opportunities they move toward afterward.

MOVING FORWARD

Turn the experience into action.

The fullest measure of impact is when opportunity comes full circle - when someone who was once served is eventually able to return, contribute and open a door for someone coming behind them.

AVIATION

FLIGHT IS MORE THAN THE DESTINATION. IT’S THE EXPOSURE.

Aviation is From Foster to Flight’s signature pathway because sometimes expanding a young person’s future begins by introducing them to a world they were never given the opportunity to see. Through aviation, young people can be exposed to aircraft, airports, pilots, aviation professionals and the wide range of careers that exist throughout the industry - turning something that may have once felt distant or unfamiliar into something they can begin to see themselves pursuing.

The goal is bigger than taking a young person on a flight. Aviation becomes a vehicle for mentorship, career exploration, education and access - connecting interested youth with professionals, experiences and information that can help them understand what it actually takes to enter the field and determine whether aviation belongs in their own future.

For young people who discover that it does, From Foster to Flight creates tangible pathways toward deeper aviation education, mentorship, training and career opportunities through strategic relationships within the aviation community. For those who discover a different direction, the pathway continues through connections with educators, mentors, professionals and partners across other career fields - expanding exposure and helping young people identify opportunities aligned with their own interests, strengths and goals.

“Not every young person will choose aviation. Every young person should have the opportunity to know it was an option.”

THE BOOK

Before it became an organization, it was a life.

From Foster to Flight is Asia Payton's personal memoir and motivational story - a separate, personally owned creative work that shares the emotional origin behind the organization.

One of six children, Asia's childhood was shaped by instability, separation, an incarcerated father, abuse in her relationship with her mother, foster care and periods when survival came before dreaming. Belongings moved in trash bags. Schools, homes and relationships changed. Later came homelessness, dangerous environments, motherhood and the difficult work of deciding what kind of woman she wanted to become.

The story does not claim that one program, one mentor or one moment saved her. It follows the accumulation of choices, relationships, faith, accountability and opportunity that allowed survival to become purpose - and eventually brought her back to the same kinds of youth and systems she once navigated.

SHE CARRIED HER LIFE IN TRASH BAGS. SHE REFUSED TO LET THAT BE THE END OF HER STORY.
